newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares surge over 2 pct at close.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares surge over 2 pct at close.

text.p: Singapore shares surged to close sharply higher in heavy trading on Thursday on renewed fund buying in blue chips.

Dealers said sentiment was very firm with strong gains seen in several heavyweight stocks as funds continued on their buying spree. Singapore Press foreign, Cycle & Carriage and SIA foreign rose between S$0.30 and S$0.90 cents each.

"Most of the bad news in Singapore has been discounted and funds are afraid of missing out," said a dealer. While there has been no change in fundamentals of a slowing local economy, funds are said to be buying in anticipation of a recovery next year.
The key Straits Times Industrials index jumped 43.28 points or 2.02 percent to close at 2,189.76. Volume was a hectic 232.9 million shares with 373 gainers swamping 48 losers.
An analyst with a foreign house said there was talk of U.S. hedge funds buying after Singapore's bad third quarter economic figures came out last week.
Newly listed FJ Benjamin topped actives with more than 30.6 million traded and ended sharply higher at S$1.19 against its offer price of S$0.80.
